recommendations.text: Assess severity by ability to speak, respiratory rate, pulse rate, SpO2, PEF. Mild-moderate: talks in phrases, PEF >50%. Severe: sits hunched, talks in words, PEF <50%. Life-threatening: drowsy/confused, silent chest.

For Initial Severity Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - assess severity classification (within 5 minutes) - measure peak expiratory flow (within 10 minutes) - measure oxygen saturation (within 3 minutes) - assess vital signs

During Initial Severity Assessment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give sedative, give benzodiazepine, give morphine, give beta blocker, give nonselective beta blocker, delay bronchodilator.
Converted from unconditional: mucolytics are harmful in acute asthma with hypoxia (SpO2 <92%); may worsen airway obstruction and trigger bronchospasm [FORBIDDEN: give_mucolytics] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; mucolytics may worsen bronchospasm in acute exacerbations

recommendations.text: Nebulized mucolytics like acetylcysteine trigger bronchospasm in acute asthma exacerbation, particularly dangerous with hypoxia. [FORBIDDEN: give_mucolytics_in_hypoxic_asthma, give_acetylcysteine_nebulized_in_acute_asthma] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; mucolytics worsen bronchospasm in acute exacerbation especially with hypoxia

recommendations.text: Chest physiotherapy/percussion in acute asthma increases oxygen demand and may trigger further bronchospasm. [FORBIDDEN: give_chest_physiotherapy_in_acute_asthma, perform_percussion_drainage_in_bronchospasm] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; chest physiotherapy increases oxygen demand and may worsen bronchospasm in acute asthma

recommendations.text: Routine antibiotics in severe asthma without infection evidence promote resistance and delay appropriate treatment. [FORBIDDEN: give_routine_antibiotics_in_viral_asthma, give_empiric_azithromycin_without_infection_evidence] (Severity: MODERATE)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; antibiotics not indicated for asthma exacerbation without bacterial infection evidence

recommendations.text: IV theophylline/aminophylline in acute asthma has narrow therapeutic index with seizure and arrhythmia risk. [FORBIDDEN: give_iv_theophylline_in_acute_asthma, give_aminophylline_in_acute_exacerbation] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; theophylline/aminophylline not recommended in acute asthma due to narrow therapeutic index and toxicity

recommendations.text: For mild-moderate exacerbations: salbutamol 4-10 puffs via pMDI/spacer, repeated every 20 minutes for first hour. Add oral corticosteroids early (prednisolone 40-50 mg or equivalent).

For Mild-Moderate Exacerbation Treatment, the following actions are mandatory: - give salbutamol nebulized (within 10 minutes) - give ipratropium nebulized - give systemic corticosteroid (within 60 minutes) - administer oxygen to target 94 98
During Mild-Moderate Exacerbation Treatment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give sedative, give benzodiazepine, give morphine, give beta blocker.
Converted from unconditional: mucolytics may worsen cough and airway obstruction during acute exacerbation [FORBIDDEN: give_mucolytics] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; mucolytics not recommended in acute asthma exacerbations

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: chest physiotherapy can worsen bronchospasm and increase oxygen demand during acute exacerbation [FORBIDDEN: give_chest_physiotherapy] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; chest physiotherapy not recommended in acute asthma

recommendations.text: NSAIDs and aspirin trigger severe bronchospasm in aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (AERD) via COX-1 inhibition and leukotriene overproduction. [FORBIDDEN: give_nsaid, give_aspirin, give_ibuprofen, give_ketorolac] (Severity: CRITICAL)
Patients on chronic oral corticosteroids have adrenal suppression and require stress-dose hydrocortisone (100 mg IV) during acute illness. [REQUIRED: give_stress_dose_steroids] (Severity: HIGH)

Steroid-dependent asthma patients have HPA axis suppression; stress-dose steroids are mandatory, abrupt withdrawal causes crisis. [FORBIDDEN: withhold_stress_dose_steroid_in_dependent, abruptly_stop_chronic_steroid_in_exacerbation] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024; steroid-dependent patients have adrenal suppression; abrupt withdrawal causes adrenal crisis

recommendations.text: For severe exacerbations: continuous nebulized salbutamol, ipratropium bromide, IV corticosteroid, IV magnesium sulfate 2g over 20 minutes (single infusion). Consider ICU admission.

For Severe Exacerbation Treatment, the following actions are mandatory: - give continuous salbutamol nebulized (within 10 minutes) - give ipratropium nebulized - give systemic corticosteroid iv (within 30 minutes) - administer oxygen high flow - give magnesium sulfate iv (within 30 minutes)
During Severe Exacerbation Treatment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give sedative, give benzodiazepine, give morphine, give beta blocker, delay bronchodilator.
Converted from unconditional: mucolytics are harmful in severe asthma with hypoxia (SpO2 <92%); worsen airway obstruction [FORBIDDEN: give_mucolytics] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; mucolytics contraindicated in severe asthma with hypoxia

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: chest physiotherapy worsens bronchospasm and increases oxygen demand in severe exacerbation with hypoxia [FORBIDDEN: give_chest_physiotherapy] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; chest physiotherapy contraindicated in severe asthma

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: theophylline/aminophylline has narrow therapeutic index and adds no benefit over inhaled bronchodilators in acute exacerbation [FORBIDDEN: give_theophylline_in_acute] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; theophylline not recommended in acute asthma due to toxicity risk

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: routine antibiotics provide no benefit in asthma exacerbations unless concurrent bacterial infection confirmed [FORBIDDEN: give_antibiotics_routine] (Severity: MODERATE)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; antibiotics not routinely indicated for asthma exacerbations

recommendations.text: IV magnesium sulfate (2g over 20 min) reduces admissions in severe asthma with PEF <25% or SpO2 <92%; smooth muscle relaxation via calcium antagonism. [REQUIRED: give_magnesium_sulfate_iv] (Severity: HIGH)

Life-threatening asthma requires IV MgSO4 as adjunct; bronchodilators alone are insufficient for severe exacerbation. [FORBIDDEN: discharge_severe_exacerbation_without_mgso4, give_only_bronchodilator_in_life_threatening] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024; severe/life-threatening exacerbation requires IV MgSO4 as adjunctive bronchodilator

recommendations.text: Positive pressure ventilation in pneumothorax causes tension pneumothorax and hemodynamic collapse; tube thoracostomy must precede positive pressure. [FORBIDDEN: give_niv, give_bipap, give_cpap, give_positive_pressure_ventilation] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; BTS 2015 Spontaneous Pneumothorax Guidelines

recommendations.text: Antibiotics are only indicated for asthma exacerbations with confirmed bacterial coinfection (pneumonia, sinusitis); routine antibiotics are NOT recommended. [REQUIRED: give_antibiotics] (Severity: MODERATE)

Antibiotics are only indicated for confirmed bacterial infection in asthma exacerbation; fluoroquinolone overuse promotes resistance. [FORBIDDEN: give_fluoroquinolone_without_clear_indication, withhold_antibiotics_in_confirmed_pneumonia] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024; routine antibiotics for asthma exacerbation are not recommended unless clear bacterial infection is present

recommendations.text: Life-threatening asthma (drowsy, confused, silent chest, cyanosis, feeble respiratory effort): immediate intubation and ICU. IM epinephrine if IV access unavailable. Ketamine is preferred induction agent for RSI.

For Near-Fatal Asthma Treatment, the following actions are mandatory: - give epinephrine im (within 5 minutes) - perform endotracheal intubation (within 15 minutes) - give systemic corticosteroid iv (within 15 minutes) - give magnesium sulfate iv - admit to icu (within 15 minutes)

During Near-Fatal Asthma Treatment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give sedative, give benzodiazepine, give morphine, give beta blocker, discharge home, delay intubation.
Converted from unconditional: mucolytics are harmful in near-fatal asthma; worsen airway obstruction in critically ill patients [FORBIDDEN: give_mucolytics] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; mucolytics contraindicated in near-fatal asthma

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: succinylcholine in hyperkalemic patients and histamine-releasing agents during RSI are contraindicated in asthma; use rocuronium and ketamine instead [FORBIDDEN: give_succinylcholine_if_hyperkalemic, use_rapid_sequence_with_histamine_releasers] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; succinylcholine may worsen hyperkalemia; histamine releasers worsen bronchospasm

recommendations.text: Near-fatal asthma with SpO2 <85% or imminent respiratory arrest requires IM epinephrine as rescue; bronchospasm prevents nebulized drug delivery. [REQUIRED: give_epinephrine_im] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Ketamine is the preferred induction agent for RSI in status asthmaticus due to bronchodilatory properties; propofol and thiopental lack this advantage. [REQUIRED: give_ketamine_for_induction] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: GINA 2024 Section 4.3; Goyal S, Indian J Crit Care Med 2014

recommendations.text: Undertreated asthma in pregnancy causes fetal hypoxia; all standard acute treatments (SABA, steroids, oxygen) are safer than uncontrolled asthma. [FORBIDDEN: withhold_treatment, delay_treatment, restrict_fluid] (Severity: HIGH)

Before discharge: prescribe oral corticosteroid course (5-7 days), ensure ICS is prescribed or continued, check inhaler technique, provide written asthma action plan, arrange follow-up within 2-7 days.
For Disposition Decision, the following actions are mandatory: - reassess after treatment (within 60 minutes) - determine disposition (within 240 minutes)

During Disposition Decision, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: discharge without corticosteroid prescription, discharge without followup, discharge without action plan.
